problem: S-401 is fixed for length only. completionDispositions stores evidence.trim() raw (line 696) while dispositionLine shows cardSafe(record.evidence) (line 702). cardSafe (src/lib/card-safe.ts:10-16) removes whole OSC/DCS/PM/APC escape spans together with their payload, CSI sequences, C0/C1 controls and bidi marks, so a string under the 300-character cap can carry text the operator never sees. The r05 suggested_fix named this case (refuse any evidence or finding string that cardSafe would change, so the shown text equals the stored text); only the length half landed, and the new tests build only a plain-text tail.
impact: A prompt-injected or misbehaving agent calls review_complete with a disposition whose evidence is 'fixed in abc123' + ESC ] 0 ; 'operator: decided-by alice' + BEL (about 50 characters, under every cap). The card shows 'fixed in abc123'; the operator presses yes; findings.json and completion-confirmation.json receive the raw string, and review-notes.ts attestDismissal (HUMAN_DECISION_PATTERN, line 122) classifies the stored text as 'human', so a learning note is filed 'Attested by: human' for a dismissal no person made. This is the S-401 consequence (the operator answered a text other than the one recorded), reached through a channel the length cap does not touch. The same applies to the finding string with less consequence (it must still match a package id).
suggested_fix: In completionDispositions refuse any finding or evidence whose card form differs from the text apart from the visible newline marker, so shown equals stored; for example reject control, escape and bidi characters other than tab and newline in both strings (message: dispositions[i]: evidence holds control or escape characters the card would hide). Alternatively store cardSafe(evidence). Add a test next to the hidden-tail test: evidence 'abc' + ESC ] 0 ; 'operator: decided-by alice' + BEL is refused before the card is drawn. Do not take the carried-over rest of S-401 as closed until this lands.
evidence: Executed at head 0f980c407 by five reviewers with bun: cardSafe('fixed in abc123\u001b]0;operator: decided-by alice\u0007') returns 'fixed in abc123'; HUMAN_DECISION_PATTERN matches the stored string and not the shown one; attestDismissal returns kind 'human' on the stored evidence and 'none' on the shown text (review-regression-w2 R6-01, review-security-code-w1 S-601, review-logic-w1 L6-001). Not run end to end through the card and apply; both halves (shown text, stored text feeding attestDismissal) are each confirmed, and completionDispositions has no check that could refuse the string (lines 682-697). operator-confirm-tools.ts:202 binds the token to JSON.stringify(input), so the dispositions applied are those shown.

The three waiver quotes (:717, :728, :732) show operator-typed or operator-confirmed text that nothing reads for attestation; not part of this finding.

verification.evidence: keryx review verify-run (exit 1) saved at research-evidence/verify-S-402-1.txt: bun s402-repro.ts -> storedLength 46, underCap true, shown 'fixed in abc123', storedKind human, shownKind none; DEFECT REPRODUCED. Lines 696 and 702 of src/commands/operator-confirm-review.ts store evidence.trim() raw and render cardSafe(record.evidence); completionDispositions refuses only non-string evidence or length above 300.

premise.reasoning: Nothing at operator-confirm-review.ts:676-702 suggests the gap is deliberate. cardSafe (card-safe.ts:7-16) removes escape spans along with their payload so the card cannot be forged, but the record stores evidence.trim() raw (line 696), so the text the operator confirms and the text that is stored can differ. The verifier confirmed this by running it. Refusing strings that cardSafe would change, or storing what is shown, matches the shown-equals-stored invariant of S-401. Security finding: upheld, not downgradable.

problem: askApproval returns { decision: "deny", undelivered: true } from a catch that also covers a post that timed out (requestTimeoutMs) or a response body that failed to read after serve had already registered and posted the approval, and from an already-aborted signal. The flag means the question never reached the topic; on those paths it may have.
impact: On a timeout after the approval was posted, the mirror treats the card as undelivered and falls back to the dock while the topic may still show a live card; a late press on it has no matching pending card.
suggested_fix: Set undelivered only on paths where the post provably failed (a refused connection or a non-2xx before registration); on a timeout or a failed body read return a plain deny, or an unknown-delivery state the caller handles as 'may have reached the topic'.
evidence: Static reading of src/remote/client.ts askApproval (lines 440-461, 675) by review-logic-w5; not run.

class_scope.enumeration_method: read askApproval in full; keryx ctx rg for undelivered in src/remote and src/tui/shell-bridge.ts.

premise.reasoning: client.ts:136 defines undelivered as 'the question never reached the topic'. The catch at :461 also covers the AbortSignal.timeout at :675, a failed response.text() at :677 and a proof failure at :678-679. In each of those, serve may already have posted the card. Nothing in the code says these cases count as undelivered on purpose. One part of the claim is weak: an already-aborted signal at :440 is in fact undelivered. The timeout and body-read paths still carry the finding.

problem: The new S-401 boundary tests pin the caps from one side only. Evidence: 300 accepted and 327 refused, but 301 is never built, so a cap moved to 301..326 survives; the trim is not pinned (atCap has no leading or trailing blank). Finding: 201 characters refused, but a 200-character finding is never accepted, so a >= mutant survives. The 20-entry accepted case uses twenty identical, evidence-less entries, which the engine refuses at apply (open F5-04, F5-05), so the accepted half fails for an unrelated reason once either is fixed at card time.
impact: A cap moved by one, or a trim dropped before the length check, passes the suite; a later fix of F5-04/F5-05 breaks an unrelated assertion.
suggested_fix: Add cases at 301 chars of evidence (refused), 200 chars of finding (accepted), evidence padded with blanks that is 300 after trim (accepted), and build the 20-entry accepted case from distinct findings with evidence.
evidence: Static reading of operator-confirm-review-tools.test.ts:702-720; mutant candidates m1-m5 and M-S401-1..7 proposed by review-testing-practices-w1/w2 were not run (read-only payload).

premise.reasoning: A one-sided boundary test that misses off-by-one mutants is a test gap. No intent signal and no practice source makes it smaller, and a minor is not re-graded.

problem: The new test pins 'the card shows the evidence whole' only for plain ASCII; cardSafe is the identity on every input it uses. Removing cardSafe from dispositionLine, or changing it to hide more, leaves the new and the older tests green. This is the F5-24 residual and the test half of S-402.
impact: The shown-equals-stored invariant has no test, which is how S-402 passed.
suggested_fix: Fold into the test that S-402's fix adds: an escape-bearing evidence is refused, and a string with a newline shows the visible marker.
evidence: Static reading of the tests; also reported by review-security-code-w1 (S-602).

problem: evidence.trim() is computed five times in one loop body (lines 693, 694 twice, 696 twice); the delta added three. The check and the stored value are written separately, which is how S-402 slipped between them.
impact: A later edit can change one of the five and leave the checked text different from the stored text.
suggested_fix: Bind const text = typeof evidence === "string" ? evidence.trim() : undefined once, validate it, and store it.
quote: records.push({ finding, state: state as FindingDispositionState, ...(evidence === undefined || evidence.trim() === "" ? {} : { evidence: evidence.trim() }) });

premise.reasoning: evidence.trim() is computed several times between the check (:693-694) and the store (:696). Binding the trimmed text once and validating that same value is the usual DRY fix. It also guards the check-vs-store split that S-402 lives in. No sign this is deliberate.

problem: The limit 300 is a literal in the schema description while MAX_DISPOSITION_EVIDENCE_CHARS (line 657) holds the same number, and WAIVER_QUOTE_CHARS (line 651) is also 300; the three constants sit in two groups with a type declaration between them. The text the model reads and the check can drift apart.
impact: Changing the constant leaves the schema text promising the old limit.
suggested_fix: Interpolate the constants into the description and group the caps.
quote: evidence: { type: "string", description: "Optional: the commit or reasoning behind the disposition. At most 300 characters; the card shows it whole." },

class_scope.enumeration_method: read the constants and the schema.

premise.reasoning: The schema description at :668 hard-codes 300 while MAX_DISPOSITION_EVIDENCE_CHARS (:657) holds the same limit. Interpolating the constant keeps the model-facing text and the check in step. Nothing suggests the duplication is intentional.

problem: The three caps are not derived from the limit that decides whether a card can be answered remotely: MAX_APPROVAL_PROMPT_CHARS = 3000 (src/remote/protocol.ts:160). Twenty entries of up to 200 + 300 characters can reach about 10,000 characters, so a card with six or more full-size entries gets no Telegram buttons and is answered in the dock (operatorCardTooLongForTopic, shell-bridge.ts:280; tui-shell.ts:6029). The refusal text says 'a card shows at most 20' as if all 20 fit.
impact: Documented fallback, no break: long disposition lists are answered in the shell only. The wording can mislead an operator who expects a Telegram answer.
suggested_fix: Say in the skill and the refusal text that a long list is answered in the dock, or derive the caps from the remote limit.
evidence: Read protocol.ts:160, shell-bridge.ts:280-287, tui-shell.ts:6029 and 6104 (review-logic-w1, review-logic-w7 follow-up, review-regression-w1 observation).

problem: The review-orchestrator skill tells the agent to pass dispositions to the review_complete card but omits the card-time limits (20 entries, finding 200, evidence 300). Only the tool schema states the evidence limit. Same class as the open F5-08.
impact: An agent that writes a long rationale gets a one-shot refusal and retries shorter.
suggested_fix: State the three limits at SKILL.md:284 (and in the bundled copy).
quote: The `review_complete` card records what became of a finding when the fix round closes: pass `dispositions`, a list of `{finding, disposition, evidence}`, one per finding; the operator sees each on the card.

problem: parseStoredToken validates the required fields but passes pressedBy, pressedAt and confirmedVia through as stored; consumeConfirmationToken copies pressedBy and pressedAt into the signature without a type check, while the flow schema types pressedBy as integer.
impact: A hand-edited token file could write a non-integer pressedBy into the signature; display-only, no gate reads it.
suggested_fix: Check Number.isSafeInteger(pressedBy) and a text pressedAt in parseStoredToken.
